bug_semantics: After the interactive TUI stops, gdu writes filesystem paths to the real terminal with fmt.Fprintf and no control-character stripping. Pressing Q prints ui.currentDirPath; quitting after marking items prints each marked path. tview already sanitizes on-screen rendering, but these post-Stop() writes go to os.Stdout, so a crafted directory or file name containing OSC/CSI escape sequences is interpreted by the victim terminal (title spoofing, clipboard manipulation, or other terminal-dependent effects).
flaw_origin: 30356670ad7f9b4154f78bcb97c2e97de34aeb4e first added the Q-key handler that stops the TUI then fmt.Fprintf(ui.output, "%s\n", ui.currentDirPath) with no sanitization, plus the io.Writer output field. Parent 064c8eeda80afa04aa955fdace1f037f5e2f27d4 only stopped the app on 'q' and never printed a path. Later c6207db5e4611efe7c2ace35869992a80693a75a added a second unsanitized sink (printMarkedPaths). ee9e4e27e55a9acf34ee04f350a024be9face3de only extracted the existing print into doQuit. 5d76fab735f190fd645896de90ac9982b6382aeb (PR #616) added sanitizePathForDisplay at both sinks.

reasoning: The vulnerability is CWE-116: unsanitized filesystem paths written to the terminal after tview has released the screen. The smallest first-write of that mechanism is 30356670, which introduced the documented Q-to-print-current-dir feature and the stdout sink. The parent lacks both the print and the output field. Later marked-path printing (c6207db5) is a second instance of the same missing sanitization, not the original introduction. ee9e4e27 is a move of the existing Fprintf into doQuit, so it is not a BIC despite Claude trailers. AI is judged only from 30356670: human author/committer Daniel Milde, no AI/bot markers, therefore NOT_AI. The sanitizer lands in 5d76fab / f1d803d.
